study_design: Population-based case-control study conducted in three Canadian geographic areas.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: This relationship was examined in a case-control study conducted in 3 geographical areas of Canada [Metropolitan Toronto (Ontario), Montreal (Quebec), and Vancouver (British Columbia)] with 617 incident cases and 637 population controls.
reason: The abstract evaluates incident prostate cancer overall in a case-control study but does not report an aggressive, advanced, high-grade, metastatic, or lethal incident endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: In age- and energy-adjusted models for all centers combined, the odds ratio (OR) for the highest quintile of total alcohol intake was 0.89.
estimate_classifications.reason: This is an overall prostate cancer estimate for total alcohol intake, with no aggressive-disease qualifier.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Whereas coffee and cola intake was not associated with prostate cancer, a decrease in risk was observed with tea intake of more than 500 g per day (OR 0.70).
estimate_classifications.reason: The tea estimate concerns prostate cancer overall and is not identified as an aggressive endpoint.
